title: Spinal cord stimulation attenuates itch-like behavior and dermatitis: Contribution of a spinal inhibitory neuronal ensemble and associated reductions in GRPR and sympathetic signaling
title_zh: 脊髓刺激减轻瘙痒样行为和皮炎：脊髓抑制神经元集群及其对GRPR和交感信号的相关降低作用
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic inflammatory itch is sustained by reciprocal interactions among pruriceptive circuits, scratching-induced skin injury, immune-cell infiltration, and autonomic neuroimmune signaling. Spinal cord stimulation is known to reshape dorsal horn sensory processing, but whether it modulates neuroimmune inflammation during dermatitis-associated itch remains unclear. METHODS: Using acute pruritogen-evoked itch and DNFB-induced chronic dermatitis models in mice, we examined the effects of low- and high-frequency spinal cord stimulation (LF- and HF-SCS) on itch-like behavior, skin inflammation, spinal Gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR)-associated neuronal activation, and sympathetic-associated neuroimmune changes. Activity-dependent FosTRAP2 labeling combined with chemogenetic activation or inhibition was used to test the functional contribution of the HF-SCS/TRAP-defined neuronal ensemble. RESULTS: Spinal cord stimulation reduced pruritogen-evoked licking/biting and chronic DNFB-associated itch-like behavior, accompanied by decreased epidermal hyperplasia, T-cell infiltration, and IL-1β/TNF-α-associated inflammatory signals in lesional skin. HF-SCS increased c-Fos expression within a prominent Pax2+ inhibitory neuronal component in the dorsal horn. Chemogenetic reactivation of the HF-SCS/TRAP-defined neuronal ensemble recapitulated the behavioral and cutaneous effects associated with SCS, whereas chemogenetic inhibition impaired the protective efficacy of SCS. SCS was also associated with reduced GRPR-related neuronal activation and Grpr expression. Anatomical tracing indicated an association between the HF-SCS/TRAP-defined neuronal ensemble and ChAT+ sympathetic preganglionic neurons, while HF-SCS was accompanied by reduced sympathetic-associated markers in skin and the spinal intermediolateral region. CONCLUSION: These findings identify spinal cord stimulation as a preclinical neuromodulatory approach that attenuates dermatitis-associated itch and cutaneous neuroinflammation. The data support a functional contribution of the HF-SCS/TRAP-defined neuronal ensemble, which is enriched in Pax2+ inhibitory neurons, while the reductions in GRPR-related activity and sympathetic-associated signaling remain associative findings.
abstract_zh: 背景：慢性炎症性瘙痒由瘙痒感受回路、抓挠导致的皮肤损伤、免疫细胞浸润以及自主神经-免疫信号的相互作用维持。脊髓刺激已知能重塑背角的感觉处理，但其是否调节与皮炎相关的瘙痒期间的神经免疫炎症尚不清楚。方法：利用小鼠急性瘙痒诱导剂和DNFB诱导的慢性皮炎模型，研究低频和高频脊髓刺激（LF‑SCS 与 HF‑SCS）对瘙痒样行为、皮肤炎症、脊髓胃泌素释放肽受体（GRPR）相关神经元激活以及交感神经相关神经免疫变化的影响。采用依赖活动的 FosTRAP2 标记结合化学遗传激活或抑制，检验 HF‑SCS/TRAP 定义的神经元集群的功能贡献。结果：脊髓刺激降低了瘙痒诱导剂引起的舔咬行为和 DNFB 相关的慢性瘙痒样行为，并伴随表皮增生、T 细胞浸润以及受损皮肤中 IL‑1β/TNF‑α 相关炎症信号的下降。HF‑SCS 在背角显著的 Pax2+ 抑制性神经元组中增加了 c‑Fos 表达。对 HF‑SCS/TRAP 定义的神经元集群进行化学遗传再激活，重现了 SCS 的行为和皮肤效应；相反，化学遗传抑制削弱了 SCS 的保护效能。SCS 还伴随 GRPR 相关神经元激活和 Grpr 表达的降低。解剖追踪显示 HF‑SCS/TRAP 定义的神经元集群与 ChAT+ 交感前神经元相关，而 HF‑SCS 同时伴随皮肤和脊髓中间外侧区交感相关标记的降低。结论：这些发现表明脊髓刺激是一种前临床神经调制方法，可减轻皮炎相关瘙痒和皮肤神经炎症。数据支持 HF‑SCS/TRAP 定义的神经元集群（富含 Pax2+ 抑制性神经元）的功能贡献，而 GRPR 相关活动和交感相关信号的降低仍为关联性发现。
